answer: Custody is bound to one serial history per identity, and the release schedule rewards depth of a single chain rather than the number of chains, so splitting a chain into siblings destroys the compounding the schedule was meant to reward. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. Picture a sable that only one identity owns, an opal that must pass before anything is returned, and a dawn that only lands on the survivor: a fleet buys many sable, waits many opal, and still collects one dawn per identity.
